title: 31 CFR 1010.100(ff) Money services business; (ff)(5) Money transmitter; (ff)(8) Limitation
effective_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-11-20
summary: Money transmission = acceptance of currency/funds/value from one person and transmission to another location or person by any means, plus catch-all 'any other person engaged in the transfer of funds'. Facts and circumstances. Exclusions include network/communication providers (A), payment processors for goods/services/bills through clearance systems by agreement with creditor/seller (B), and funds transfers integral to a non-transmission service (F).

title: FIN-2019-G001 Application of FinCEN's Regulations to Certain Business Models Involving Convertible Virtual Currencies (May 9, 2019)
pinpoint: §2 pp.8-9 (exemptions a-f; 'FinCEN interprets these exemptions strictly'); §4.2 p.15 (four criteria incl. 'total independent control over the value'); §4.5.1(a)-(b) pp.18-19 (integral exemption; software/tool suppliers 'engaged in trade and not money transmission'); §4.6 pp.21-22 (payment processor exemption four conditions a-d, fn 66-67)
summary: Payment-processor exemption requires: (a) facilitating purchase of goods/services or bill payment; (b) operating through clearance/settlement systems admitting only BSA-regulated institutions; (c) formal agreement; (d) agreement at minimum with the seller/creditor that receives funds. Suppliers of software tools are not money transmitters; intermediary status turns on ownership, storage, owner interaction and total independent control. Exemptions read strictly.

title: FIN-2014-R009 Application of Money Services Business Regulations to a Company Acting as an Independent Sales Organization and Payment Processor (Aug. 27, 2014)
pinpoint: Ruling text: 'As an ISO, the Company does not take possession or control of merchant funds at any point'; customers 'mostly made of non-profit and religious organizations that collect donations'; 'it appears that your activity meets conditions (a), (c) and (d)'
summary: ISO that never takes possession or control of funds is not a money transmitter. For a processor whose customers are mostly nonprofits collecting donations, FinCEN treated conditions (a),(c),(d) of the payment-processor exemption as apparently met; exemption fails if disbursement occurs outside a BSA-regulated-only clearance system.

title: 2022-2026 Money Transmission Modernization Act Proposed and Enacted Legislation (August 2026)
pinpoint: Enactment lists by year: Texas S.B. 895/H.B. 3573 full MTMA eff. 9/1/2023; California A.B. 1116 partial (exemptions, net worth...) eff. 1/1/2025 and A.B. 1498 (2022); no New York or Florida enactment listed
summary: State-by-state MTMA enactments 2022-2026. Texas full MTMA; California partial; New York and Florida not listed as enacted. 2026 introductions (AK, DE, LA, MI, OK) and payroll-processor exemptions noted.

title: CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act (MTMA) overview page
pinpoint: Page text: 'To date, thirty-one states have enacted the law in full or in part.'
summary: CSBS states 31 states have enacted the MTMA in full or in part as of November 2026 (a law-firm summary reports 35; counting methods differ).

title: Money Transmission Modernization Act (model law text)
pinpoint: §2.01(q) 'Money transmission' (selling/issuing payment instruments; stored value; 'Receiving money for transmission from a person located in this state'; excludes 'provision solely of online or telecommunications services or network access'); §3.01(a) payment-system operator; §3.01(b) agent of payee (written agreement; held out; payment treated as received by payee)
summary: Model act defines money transmission around receiving money for transmission and excludes solely providing online/telecom services or network access; agent-of-payee exemption limited to payments for goods or services with three conditions.

title: Cal. Fin. Code §2010(l) (Money Transmission Act exemption: agent of payee)
issuer: California Legislature (via california.public.law mirror; leginfo returned 403)
summary: Exempts transaction where recipient is agent of payee under preexisting written contract and delivery to agent satisfies payor's obligation; payee/payor defined by reference to goods or services. Official site not reachable; mirror text.

title: DFPI interpretive opinion letter, June 9, 2022: agent of payee for NPO donations; operating-account funds not stored value
issuer: California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation
pinpoint: §II.A pp.2-3 and §III; fn 5 citing Cal. Code Regs. tit. 10 §80.126.30 eff. 10/1/2021
summary: 'Services' clarified by regulation to include charitable activities of 501(c)(3) organizations; a rewards company receiving funds as the NPO's appointed agent under a written agreement qualifies for agent-of-payee exemption; NPO donations not regulated activity.

title: Final Statement of Reasons for Adoption of Rules under the California Money Transmission Act (PRO 07-17)
pinpoint: pp.1-2: §80.126.30 ('services' include 501(c)(3) charitable activities); 10 CCR §80.3002(a)(2) exemption for 501(c)(3) public benefit nonprofits; Fin. Code §2030 agent-of-exempt-entity analysis; rejection of common-law agency alone
summary: Charities' payment processors must meet statutory agent-of-payee requirements; common-law agency alone is insufficient; 501(c)(3) public benefit nonprofits engaging in money transmission are exempt under 10 CCR 80.3002(a)(2).

title: N.Y. Banking Law §641(1)
summary: No person may engage in the business of selling/issuing checks or receiving money for transmission or transmitting the same without a license; agents permitted only as agent of a licensee or agent of a payee; banks and certain institutions excluded.

title: NY Banking Dept interpretive letter, July 9, 2007 (processor of tax/tuition/school meal payments)
issuer: New York State Banking Department (now DFS)
pinpoint: Letter text on credit card payments going 'directly from the credit card account to an account owned by the intended payee'
summary: Where payments flow directly from payor's account to an account owned by the payee, there is no receipt of money for transmission by the processor under §641; otherwise processor must be clearly agent of payee with no risk of loss to payor.

title: Fla. Stat. §560.103(27) 'Money transmitter' (2026 Florida Statutes)
summary: Money transmitter = entity that receives currency/monetary value etc. to act as intermediary to transmit; 'The term includes only an intermediary that has the ability to unilaterally execute or indefinitely prevent a transaction.' No agent-of-payee language in §560.103.

title: Texas S.B. 895 (88R) enrolled bill analysis (MTMA adoption; Tex. Fin. Code ch. 152)
pinpoint: Analysis of Sec. 152.004(2) agent-of-payee exemption (written agreement; held out; payment treated as received by payee); Sec. 152.003 definitions
summary: Texas adopted MTMA structure; agent-of-payee exemption at Fin. Code §152.004(2) mirrors MTMA §3.01(b). Statute text itself not fetched (site is a JS app).

title: Investment Company Act §3(c)(10), 15 U.S.C. 80a-3(c)(10)
pinpoint: §3(c)(10)(A)-(D), esp. (B)(i) 'assets of the general endowment fund or other funds of one or more charitable organizations' and (D)(i) definition of 'maintained'
summary: Excludes funds maintained by a charitable organization for collective investment of assets of one or more charitable organizations; 'maintained' if the charity serves as trustee or administrator or has power to remove and designate trustees/administrators.

title: Investment Company Act §7(e), 15 U.S.C. 80a-7(e)
summary: Each §3(c)(10)(B) fund must provide each donor, at the time of donation, written information describing the material terms of the operation of the fund.

title: Securities Act §3(a)(4), 15 U.S.C. 77c(a)(4)
summary: Exempts securities of charitable issuers and any security of a fund excluded under ICA §3(c)(10)(B).

title: Exchange Act §3(e), 15 U.S.C. 78c(e)
pinpoint: §3(e)(1) charitable organization not a broker/dealer when trading for itself or a §3(c)(10)(B) fund; §3(e)(2) Limitation on compensation
summary: Charity broker/dealer exemption is unavailable unless each person soliciting donations to a §3(c)(10)(B) fund is a volunteer or engaged in overall fundraising and receives no commission or special compensation based on number or value of donations collected for the fund. Exemption covers the charity and its personnel only.

title: Investment Advisers Act §202(a)(11), 15 U.S.C. 80b-2(a)(11)
summary: Investment adviser: for compensation, in the business of advising others on value/advisability of securities, or as part of a regular business issuing analyses or reports concerning securities; exclusions include bona fide publishers (D).

title: Investment Advisers Act §203(b)(4), 15 U.S.C. 80b-3(b)(4)
summary: Registration exemption for an adviser that is a charitable organization (or its trustee, director, officer, employee or volunteer) advising only charities, §3(c)(10)(B) funds, or related donative trusts and their settlors/beneficiaries. Does not cover a for-profit vendor.

title: Release IA-1092, Applicability of the Investment Advisers Act to Financial Planners, Pension Consultants, and Other Persons (Oct. 1987)
effective_date: 1987-10-08 (date not re-read; PDF OCR partially garbled)
pinpoint: §II.2 'Business' standard pp.8-10 (holding out; separate compensation or transaction-based compensation; specific investment advice other than rare, isolated, non-periodic); §II.3 Compensation p.10 (OCR unreadable; 'any economic benefit' language cited from memory)
summary: Staff test: person is 'in the business' if it holds itself out as adviser, receives separate or transaction-based compensation for advice, or gives specific investment advice (incl. percentage allocations to particular fund types) other than rarely. Generic allocation advice excluded.

title: Lowe v. SEC, 472 U.S. 181 (1985)
pinpoint: Opinion of the Court (Stevens, J.) discussing §202(a)(11)(D) publisher exclusion
summary: Bona fide publications of general and regular circulation offering impersonal advice are excluded; personalized advice 'attuned to any specific portfolio or to any client's particular needs' identifies an investment adviser.

title: Guide to Broker-Dealer Registration (April 2008)
issuer: SEC Division of Trading and Markets
summary: Broker = engaged in business of effecting transactions in securities for the account of others; indicators include compensation depending on outcome/size of transactions, handling funds or securities of others, and operating platforms to trade securities.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4958(c)(2), (f)(1)(E)-(F), (f)(7), (f)(8)
summary: Any grant, loan, compensation or similar payment from a DAF to a donor/advisor (or family/35% entity) is an excess benefit in full. Investment advisors compensated by a sponsor for managing or advising on DAF assets are disqualified persons of the sponsor.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4966(d)(2) donor advised fund definition
summary: DAF advisor includes any person appointed or designated by the donor who has or reasonably expects advisory privileges over distribution or investment.

title: Taxes on Taxable Distributions From Donor Advised Funds Under Section 4966 (proposed rule) 88 FR 77922
pinpoint: 88 FR 77926, Explanation of Provisions §1.C (personal investment advisor as donor-advisor; proposed §53.4966-1(h)(3))
summary: Proposal would treat a sponsor-compensated personal investment advisor managing a DAF as a donor-advisor while in that dual capacity, making DAF payments to it subject to §4958(c)(2). Not effective law.

title: Status of REG-142338-07 (search results: Council on Foundations page updated 2026-05-08; EY Oct 2025 priority guidance plan)
summary: No source found reporting finalization or withdrawal of the Nov 2023 proposed §4966 regulations as of mid/late 2026; remains on 2025-2026 Priority Guidance Plan. Not fetched; treat as proposed.

title: Cal. Gov. Code §12599.9 (charitable fundraising platforms and platform charities; AB 488)
summary: Defines charitable fundraising platform by five acts (A list charities by name; B peer-to-peer; C/D purchase-linked; E customizable website/SaaS for charities to solicit/receive donations, excluding the charity's own platform). Excludes charity's own platform, vendors solely providing technical/supportive services to a CFP, and DAF sponsors that do not list charities for non-advisors. Registration before enabling solicitations; annual reports; good standing; disclosures (A-C); consent; receipts.

title: Initial Statement of Reasons, AB 488 implementing regulations (11 CCR §§314-322)
summary: Solicitation types A-E track Gov. Code §12599.9(a)(1)(A)-(E); type E references private-labeled or customizable platforms and a software-as-a-service license agreement; requirements vary by type.

title: Final Statement of Reasons Attachment A (responses to comments), AB 488 regulations
pinpoint: Resp. 14-15 p.9 (DAF sponsor as donor); Resp. 18 p.9 (types A-E in §314(m)-(q)); Resp. ~p.12 (type E: 'a CO uses the CFP to solicit or receive donations for itself'); Resp. 7 p.~4 (CFPs 'regardless of whether they are operated by COs or for-profits'); Resp. 56-57 pp.24-25 (DAF variance power)
summary: DOJ: CFP definition covers for-profits; in type E a charity uses the CFP to solicit for itself; DAF sponsors acting as CFPs/PCs may exercise variance power under §320(a)(3).

title: Final Statement of Reasons, AB 488 regulations (Title 11, Ch. 4 and 15)
pinpoint: Section 'Effective Date of Regulations and Annual Reporting Form' (approx. p.5)
summary: Department delayed effective date of sections 318-322 to January 1, 2025; AB 488 effective January 1, 2023.

title: Cal. Gov. Code §12599 (commercial fundraiser for charitable purposes)
summary: Commercial fundraiser = any person who for compensation solicits funds in California for charitable purposes, receives/controls solicited funds, or engages compensated solicitors; excludes employees of charities, depository banks, escrow/caging, trustees/charitable corporations; must register before soliciting.

title: Cal. Gov. Code §12599.1 (fundraising counsel for charitable purposes)
summary: Fundraising counsel plans/advises but does not solicit or receive funds and is not paid by percentage; exclusions incl. investment counselor advising a client in the profession and persons under $25,000 annual compensation; registration required.

title: N.Y. Executive Law §171-a(4),(5),(9)
pinpoint: §171-a(4) professional fund raiser; (5) professional solicitor; (9) fund raising counsel
summary: Professional fund raiser includes any person who for compensation solicits on behalf of a charitable organization; bona fide charity employees excluded; fund raising counsel must not solicit or access contributions.

title: 31 CFR 1020.220 (CIP for banks) and 1020.100(b) (customer definition)
effective_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-11-20
summary: CIP is required of banks subject to AML program rules; 'customer' is the person opening a new account. Imposes no obligation on non-bank account holders or their counterparties.

title: 31 CFR 1010.230 (beneficial ownership for legal entity customers)
effective_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-11-20
summary: Nonprofit corporations filed with a state are legal entity customers subject only to the control prong of beneficial ownership identification.

title: 31 CFR 1022.210 (AML programs for money services businesses)
effective_date: eCFR up to date as of 2026-11-20
summary: Each MSB as defined in §1010.100(ff) must maintain a written risk-based AML program; obligation attaches only on MSB status.

title: OFAC Frequently Asked Questions (General) 11, 13, 15
summary: 'All U.S. persons must comply with OFAC sanctions'; compliance program guidance referenced (Framework); OFAC strongly encourages due diligence. No explicit screening mandate.

title: A Framework for OFAC Compliance Commitments (May 2, 2019)
pinpoint: p.1 (risk-based SCP; five components); p.10 §VI Sanctions Screening Software or Filter Faults
summary: OFAC strongly encourages a risk-based sanctions compliance program with management commitment, risk assessment, internal controls, testing/auditing, training; screening-software faults are a recurring root cause of violations.

title: FinCEN final rule delaying Investment Adviser AML/CFT rule to January 1, 2028 (91 FR 36, Jan. 2, 2026)
summary: Effective date of the 2024 investment adviser AML program/SAR rule (89 FR 72156) delayed to January 1, 2028. Not fetched.

title: daf-landscape REG-042 (prior research record on 31 CFR 1010.100(ff)(5) and sponsor paying its own grants)
summary: Prior internal record: sponsor paying its own grants from its own accounts through a bank is paying its own funds, not transmitting for others (labelled inference). Consistent with this dossier.
